newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LEAGUE OFFICIALS "OUT OF TOUCH," SAYS GIBSON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEAGUE OFFICIALS "OUT OF TOUCH," SAYS GIBSON.

text.p: The English premier league's top three officials are out of touch with the real football world, according to Middlesbrough chairman Steve Gibson.
F.A. Cup finalists Middlesbrough were battling for their premier league survival away to Leeds on Sunday.
Gibson launched his attack on the premier league's chairman Sir John Quinton, chief executive Peter Leaver and secretary Mike Foster in the Mail on Sunday.
"The League is being run by a former banker, a lawyer and an administrator who have no idea what the real football world is about," he was quoted as saying.
"It is time we had football people running football."

Criticising the league's decision to deduct three points from Middlesbrough for failing to fulfil a fixture against Blackburn last December, Gibson said: "If we manage to stay up after all this it will be in spite of the way they have treated us.
"We thought we were badly done to in the first place but I was convinced we had enough going for us to win the appeal. I was wrong."
